about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

exemption.reason: These bytes are the map as #207 corrected it: twenty effect entries whose span had been extended through every rule between the condition's lead and their own now quote their own sentence, and round-down quotes Round Down and not the Save entry after it, because the heading path now identifies which printing of a repeated passage a citation means (0030). Every quote is shorter and no entry's rule changed; the review owed is still the one below. Not reviewed: this is the first mapping of the Rules Glossary's fifteen conditions and it has not had the blind second mapping 0014 requires, so nothing has compared it with a second reading of pp. 177-191. The map is trial evidence for #8 and is not used for anything downstream: there is no map-package.json, nothing packs it, and no engine consumes it. `legacy` is the wrong word and is used deliberately, for the reason examples/srd-52-combat/README.md finding 8 already recorded — it is the only exemption kind that names a tracking issue, and `non-semantic` needs a reviewed map to depart from, which a new map does not have. A blind second mapping is owed before this map is packed or built from, and it should look hardest at three things this trial's own report names as unsettled: whether the fifteen hub entries are rules or a mapper's scaffolding, whether the twelve ambiguity verdicts are the right twelve (the rate, 18% of in-scope entries, is below trial 7's 27% and the report argues the genre explains it), and whether the 110 crossReferences items are complete. The SRD's declared pointerPhrases still detect none of the 51 condition-to-condition references in the slice and oblige none of them, but they are no longer the only detector: `defined-term-use` reads the fifteen names out of condition-list and obliges every naming of one outside its own passage (#249), and it reports 54 namings in 22 entries, every one declared. That is a mechanical floor under the question, not an answer to it -- whether the right entries were written, and whether their targets are the right targets, is still what the blind second mapping is for. Since those bytes, one change, for #254 (docs/decisions/0058), departing from sha256 ecdccc64840ab7fe867171a0d579c371e998915ceea283a43946f4efdec2a571: three `scope: out`, `status: declined` entries -- suffocation-hazard, dead-revival-conditions and grappling-ends -- each gain one `crossReferences` item, anchored on the bare condition name their evidence uses and resolving to the entry that defines it (`Exhaustion` -> exhaustion twice, `Grappled` -> grappled). 0026 section 1 is written from the in-scope side and did not say whether a declined out-of-scope entry owes the declaration; 0058 rules that the passage that points declares it, whatever the engine does with the rule, and the map's own practice is what settled it -- heavily-obscured and grappling-ends already declared under the same scope and status. Nothing else about any entry changes: same citation, kind, scope, status, clarity, evidence, dependsOn and note, verified field by field. It changes relations, so it carries an independent verdict rather than a non-semantic exemption, following the precedent examples/faa-part-107/review.json set for #116. The verdict is independent-verdict-254.json, which names these bytes: a reviewer in a separate context, given only the corpus pages, the before/after, an entry index, the defining entries and 0026, and told not to read the repository. It disagreed with two of the three spans in round 1 -- a span carrying a numeral and `level` names a level count, which exhaustion-levels defines, not the condition -- and both were narrowed to the bare term before round 2 agreed 3 of 3. Two findings it raised are open and filed, #400 and #401. The map as a whole is still not blind-mapped, so the exemption stays legacy for the reasons above.
